## Overview

Loads every FP8 checkpoint tensor of GLM5-next's MLA projections, the sparse-attention indexer `wk` and MiMo-V2's fused `qkv_proj` on its own, instead of holding a weight until its scale arrives. Part of the direct weight reload work (RFC #54477); builds on #64357 (merged); replaces hao-aaron/vllm#5.
## Claims

- RL weight updates split a weight from its scale across `load_weights` calls. Those updates now load correctly, in either order, with direct reload (#64336). On the base they were silently dropped, applied wrongly or raised. Layerwise reload is not supported for these layers: it is being removed (#54477), and this PR carries no layerwise-only machinery.
  - GLM-5.3-Flash (split weight/scale, direct reload with #64336, TP2): base has 8 projection weights wrong and different greedy outputs. This PR matches a fresh server.
  - MiMo-V2.6 shapes (requantize path, direct reload, TP2): this PR matches a fresh server.
- BF16 tensors under the same names still load, which is what RL trainers send.
- Cold start is unchanged: GSM8K, MTP acceptance length match the base, and KV cache is within 131 tokens of it, on GLM-5.3-Flash, GLM-5.3 FP8, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, Hy4 and MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL. Throughput is within run-order noise.
- The pairing code is removed from 14 model and MTP loader files: 715 lines added, 676 removed under `vllm/`.

## Validation

**Unit tests**, GB200, slurm 44545 on c5eecf26ff and 44562 on c8a7b6520a (and 44546 on the previous head 0accea297a: same results apart from the removed and moved tests). In CI, `test_fp8_dequant.py` runs in the H200 "Quantized Models" step, with `models/quantization`. It is not run in a CPU step: CPU builds swap `layer.weight` for a packed GEMM handle after processing. The tests import symbols this PR adds, so they cannot run on the base; the fails-before evidence is the bench below.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_fp8_dequant.py` (now including the two GLM5-next loader tests moved from `test_quark.py`, which no CI step runs) | 36 passed |
| `test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py` | 48 passed, 2 skipped (MiMo layouts the TP size does not fit) |
| `test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm52` | 10 passed, 1 skipped |
| `test_direct_reload.py` | 35 passed |
| `test_registry.py -k weights_track` (strict loaded-weights check) | 2 passed |

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8_dequant.py tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py
pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm52
```

They cover every indexer scale layout (bit-equal to the base's dequantization), weight and scale in separate calls in both orders, BF16 delivery, replicated layers, a TP 2 column-parallel slice (weight rows and scale rows), MiMo's TP slices, dummy weights, an FP8 weight whose scale never arrived (rejected at cold start), the Quark `weight_scale` name and NoPE `kv_a` padding, direct reload equal to cold start at the startup addresses, and MiMo's requantized rows byte-equal to the base's formula.

**Weight-update bench.** The [sharded-trainer bench](https://github.com/hao-aaron/vllm-state-transition-verifier/tree/sharded-trainer-bench): NCCL, trainer `fsdp=2`, server TP2 on GB200, 1 warmup + 2 measured syncs alternating two perturbed checkpoints. The trainer's packed bucket is set to 1 byte (`packed_buffer_size_bytes=1` in the NCCL trainer args, via a 7-line local patch read from `BENCH_PACKED_BUFFER_BYTES`), so every tensor arrives in its own `load_weights` call. `--audit` compares every device tensor with a fresh server on the last checkpoint; greedy outputs (4 prompts × 32 tokens) are compared too.

| Model | Reload | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash, 4 layers, FP8 indexer `wk` | direct, FP8 | 8 weights wrong; greedy 0/4 identical | 0 wrong; greedy 4/4, logprob diff 0 |
| | direct, BF16 MLA + `wk` | – | 0 wrong; greedy 4/4, diff 0 |
| MiMo-V2.6 shapes, 4 layers, requantize path | direct, FP8 | – | 0 wrong; greedy 4/4, diff 0 |

The rows ran with #64336 on both arms, before the layerwise-only machinery was removed (c5eecf26ff; it doesn't change the direct path). "Wrong" excludes the attention backends' scratch buffers (6 on GLM).

```bash
python bench/run_bench.py --model-a $MODEL --update $CKPT_1 --update $CKPT_2 --layout fsdp=2 --backend nccl \
  --server-gpus 0,1 --trainer-gpus 2,3 --warmup 1 --iters 2 --audit \
  --env VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct --env BENCH_PACKED_BUFFER_BYTES=1 -- --tensor-parallel-size 2
```

<details><summary>Fails before / passes after: split FP8 weight and scale (GLM-5.3-Flash, direct reload)</summary>

Base (#64357 + #64336 on main `255431b5e`, slurm 41176), mismatched after 3 syncs:

```
fused_qkv_a_proj.weight, indexer.wk_weights_proj.weight, o_proj.weight, q_b_proj.weight   (layer 3, ranks 0 and 1)
greedy: 0/4 prompts identical tokens, max |logprob diff| 3.45
```

This PR (slurm 41470, same checkpoints with #64692 overlaid for GLM-5's derived caches): projections all match; greedy 4/4 identical, logprob diff 0. The remaining 6 differences are attention scratch buffers (`_workspace_buffer`, `index_group`).

</details>

<details><summary>Fails before / passes after: MiMo layerwise reload</summary>

Base (slurm 41451), mismatched after 3 syncs: `qkv_proj.weight` and `qkv_proj.weight_scale_inv` of all 4 layers on both ranks (16); greedy 0/4 identical, max logprob diff 1.32. The base writes both tensors with `default_weight_loader` directly, which bypasses layerwise reload's loader wrapper.

This PR (slurm 41467): 0 mismatched; greedy 4/4 identical, diff 0.

</details>

**Cold-start A/B.** A = #64357 + #64336 on main `255431b5e`, B = this PR, on the same nightly wheel and node(s), back to back. GSM8K 5-shot greedy (1319 questions); MTP with 1 speculative token; `vllm bench serve` random 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 64. Swapped passes (B first) where throughput differed by more than 3%. A worker extension counted each module's quant-method class on both arms to confirm the new path runs.

| Model (GB200, TP) | GSM8K A → B | MTP acceptance length A → B | Output tok/s A → B | KV cache tokens A → B | Changed layers in B (per rank) |

| GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 (TP4) | 0.9113 → 0.9098 | 1.951 → 1.951 | 1435 → 1419 | 2.435M → 2.435M | 44 `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` |
| GLM-5.3 FP8 (2 nodes, TP8) | 0.9105 → 0.9166 | 1.943 → 1.944 | 1041 → 953 | 1.247M → 1.247M (−64) | 21 GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM over `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` |
| ↳ swapped | 0.9113 → 0.9121 | 1.943 → 1.943 | 739 → 866 | same | |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 (TP4) | 0.8984 → 0.9075 | 1.940 → 1.942 | 1263 → 1209 | 808k → 808k (−64) | 21 GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM over `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` |
| ↳ swapped | 0.9022 → 0.9136 | 1.942 → 1.942 | 1078 → 1230 | same | |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4, rerun on dc82144c9 (TP4) | 0.9030 → 0.9045 | 1.942 → 1.940 | 1248 → 1152 | 808k → 808k (−64) | 21, same |
| ↳ swapped | 0.9052 → 0.9067 | 1.942 → 1.942 | 1183 → 1148 | same | |
| Hy4-FP4, text model (TP4) | 0.6694 → 0.6748 | 1.000 → 1.000 | 1376 → 1193 | 417k → 417k (−64) | 21 `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` |
| ↳ swapped | 0.6823 → 0.6763 | 1.000 → 1.000 | 1108 → 1320 | same | |
| MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL (TP4) | 0.8969 → 0.8923 | 1.936 → 1.937 | 2945 → 2931 | 1.850M → 1.850M (−131) | 48 `_Fp8RowScalesLinearMethod` |

- GSM8K and acceptance length agree within noise (≤ 1.1 points; the swapped passes move by as much).
- Throughput moves by up to 15% with run order between passes of the same code. Averaged over each model's passes, B is within 2% of A: GLM-5.3 FP8 890 → 910, Hy4 1242 → 1257, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 (4 passes) 1193 → 1185, GLM-5.3-Flash and MiMo single passes −1.1% and −0.5%. B was slower in three of the four NVFP4 passes; its 21 changed layers run the same BF16 GEMM as the base, which also dequantized `wk` to BF16 at load.
- KV cache: B keeps each indexer's float32 row scale registered for reloads (172 KB per indexer layer for DeepSeek-V3.2 shapes, 192 rows × 224 groups), and MiMo keeps one scale per `qkv_proj` row. That costs 64–131 tokens of KV cache.
- Hy4's MTP accepts nothing on both arms (a property of this testing checkpoint), and its text-only config was flattened from the VL checkpoint.
- **A cold-start A/B of the current head (c5eecf26ff) on GLM-5.3-Flash and MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL is running; its results will be added here.**
- The A/B rows ran B at 52d9eeab1 (the NVFP4 rerun at dc82144c9). Later commits change the reload paths, tests and comments, and remove the sharded RDT changes. Two touch cold-start code without changing its result: MiMo's row-scale method is now adopted (`_Fp8RowScalesLinearMethod.adopt`) instead of a `__class__` swap, and the GLM-5.2 GEMM installer checks `weight.dtype`; both are covered by the unit tests.

<details><summary>A/B reproduction</summary>

```bash
AB_LABEL="GLM-5.3-NVFP4 + MTP (GB200, TP4)" AB_MODEL=$MODEL AB_TP=4 AB_SPEC=1 \
AB_SERVE='--max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
AB_A=<base worktree> AB_B=<this PR worktree> sbatch tools/ab/ab.sbatch
```

The arm script cold-starts `vllm serve`, runs GSM8K (5-shot, greedy, 1319) against it, reads acceptance length from `/metrics`, then runs `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --max-concurrency 64` and reads the KV cache size from the server log.

</details>

**Coverage.** GLM-5.3 runs the DeepSeek-V3.2 model class, so its runs cover the DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 indexer, MTP and low-latency GEMM paths. The `deepseek_v2.py` loader, `deepseek_mtp.py`, the AMD files and dots3 are checked by inspection; only their shared helpers (checkpoint names, the any-layout scale, FP8 `weights_proj`) have unit tests.

## Details

**Why.** Some loaders held a checkpoint tensor until its partner arrived: an FP8 weight waited for its scale, and the pair was dequantized or resharded inside `load_weights`. RL updates call `load_weights` once per bucket, so the pair can be split across calls, in either order. Depending on where the buffer lived, the base silently dropped the split pair (local buffer: GLM5-next, HY-V4), parked it on the GPU (buffer on the model: DeepSeek-V2/V3.2, MiMo-V2) or raised (dots3). Direct reload (#64336) also needs every checkpoint tensor to have a registered place to live.

**Design.** Each checkpoint tensor is a parameter under its checkpoint name and loads on its own. Post-load processing combines the parts in place, so addresses stay stable for CUDA graphs.

1. **GLM5-next FP8 MLA projections.** New `Fp8DequantConfig` / `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` (`layers/quantization/fp8_dequant.py`) for layers that a checkpoint stores as block FP8 but that run in BF16.
   - The weight is the BF16 weight. An FP8 tensor loads through an FP8 view of the same storage (row *i* into the first half of BF16 row *i*'s bytes), so no memory is added. Post-load processing dequantizes those rows in place, in chunks; BF16 rows and dummy weights are left alone.
   - `weight_scale_inv` is a regular block scale, retired after processing but registered for reloads.
   - `fp8_rows` (host bookkeeping on the CPU) marks the rows loaded as FP8, so post-load processing dequantizes only those.
   - The scale starts as `FP8_SCALE_SENTINEL`; at cold start, post-load processing raises if an FP8 row's scale never arrived. On a direct reload, a missing scale is caught by the update-completeness check (#54477 F2) instead.
   - Loaders only adapt single tensors: the Quark `weight_scale` name and NoPE `kv_a` padding. A BF16 tensor needs no scale; `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` marks its `weight_scale_inv` `optional_in_checkpoint`, which the opt-in strict loaded-weights check (`enable_weights_track`, `default_loader.py`) honours, so BF16 checkpoints don't report it as missing (also when the GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM wraps the layer).
2. **Indexer `wk`** (DeepSeek-V2/V3.2, HY-V4, GLM5-next, their MTPs, dots3). `wk_weights_proj` uses `Fp8DequantLinearMethod`. Checkpoints store the `wk` scale as 128×128 blocks, per channel, per tensor or MXFP8 E8M0. The layer is replicated, so its scale is one float32 per row and 32 columns, and each layout is expanded into it as it loads (widths must be multiples of 32, as the indexer's are). The `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` helpers and buffers are removed. The GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM wraps `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` layers, keeping their post-load processing.
3. **MiMo-V2 fused FP8 `qkv_proj`** (model and MTP). The checkpoint is pre-sharded for `num_key_value_heads` ranks.
   - The weight loader writes this rank's rows in the forward's layout; it needs no scale.
   - `weight_scale_inv` holds one checkpoint scale per row; its loader also records whether the rows need requantizing, which depends on the scale tiling.
   - Post-load processing (`_Fp8RowScalesLinearMethod`, adopted from the layer's `Fp8LinearMethod`) turns row scales into block scales in the same storage. Where rows form whole checkpoint blocks it takes each block's scale; otherwise it dequantizes and requantizes as the base did. It raises if the weight was loaded without its scale.
   - Both tensors are written with `default_weight_loader`, as on main; the MTP's BF16 fused branch is unchanged from main.

**Known limitations**
- MiMo `qkv_proj` must be in every update, like any block-FP8 linear layer: its post-processing (DeepGEMM on SM100) rewrites the weight and scales. A direct reload that leaves out its weight, or sends only its scale, post-processes the previous load's bytes without an error here; the update-completeness check (#54477 F2, aoshen02/vllm#176) raises for both before post-load processing runs.
- A bare `model.load_weights` of FP8 tensors without the reload lifecycle leaves FP8 bytes in those rows until post-load processing runs. BF16 tensors load and run as before. This includes the sparse NCCL engine, which runs only `finalize_model_weights` and never the layers' post-load step.
- Layerwise reload is not supported for these layers (it is being removed, #54477). A direct reload that sends FP8 rows without their scale reuses the previous scale; the update-completeness check (#54477 F2) is what rejects that.
- **Sharded RDT is not supported for these models**, on main or with this PR:
  - On main, GLM5-next fails when the engine initializes (`unhashable type: 'list'`), and DeepSeek-V3.2 fails on the second sync (`CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`). FP8 updates into these layers are refused at bake time.
  - This PR leaves the RDT engine unchanged. The fix is the load plan, #64418: its `TraceTensor` replaces the RDT bake and ignores constant writes, and RDT moves onto direct reload.
- **Out of scope: other loaders that pair checkpoint tensors across calls, left as on main because these models are not RL targets:**
  - Molmo / Molmo2 (`molmo.py`, `molmo2.py`): concatenates `wte.embedding` and `wte.new_embedding` in one call. VLM.
  - Flint (`vllm/models/flint/ops/moe.py`, `flint/model.py`): waits for all expert tensors and repacks in the loader; re-reads the GGUF. Niche NVFP4/GGUF.
  - Jina-embeddings-v3 (`bert_with_rope.py`): merges LoRA A/B into the base weight. Embedding model.
  - Reranker conversions: Qwen3-Reranker, mxbai-rerank-v2, bge-reranker-v2-gemma (`adapters.py`). They derive `score.weight` from `lm_head` rows. Pooling models.
  - BERT MLM (`bert.py`): copies the decoder from the embedding when it is absent. Encoder-only.
  - Whisper family: voxtral, ultravox, ming_audio, moss_transcribe_diarize, glmasr (`whisper.py`). They add a zero k_proj bias per call. Audio.
  - Nemotron-3.5 Transcribe (`nemotron3_5_transcribe_audio.py`): checks audio-tower completeness per call. ASR.
  - openPangu (`openpangu.py`): derives the attention sinks per call. Niche.
  - AliceAI (`alice_ai.py`): checks completeness per call. Niche.
  - FoPE / InternS1-Pro (`rotary_embedding/fope.py`): builds its cos/sin cache at the first forward. Niche.
  - ColBERT, ColPali, ColQwen3, ColQwen3.5: their loaders bypass the parameters' weight loaders. Retrieval models.
  - Drafters that are rarely updated: Qwen3 XPress, LiLiCorr, Laguna DFlash, and the Qwen3 DFlash `mask_embedding` (re-read from disk).
  - torchao and humming: direct reload refuses them.

**Coverage.** GLM-5.3 runs the DeepSeek-V3.2 model class, so its runs cover the DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 indexer, MTP and low-latency GEMM paths. The `deepseek_v2.py` loader, `deepseek_mtp.py`, the AMD files and dots3 are checked by inspection; only their shared helpers (checkpoint names, the any-layout scale, FP8 `weights_proj`) have unit tests.

## Details

**Why.** Some loaders held a checkpoint tensor until its partner arrived: an FP8 weight waited for its scale, and the pair was dequantized or resharded inside `load_weights`. RL updates call `load_weights` once per bucket, so the pair can be split across calls, in either order. Depending on where the buffer lived, the base silently dropped the split pair (local buffer: GLM5-next, HY-V4), parked it on the GPU (buffer on the model: DeepSeek-V2/V3.2, MiMo-V2) or raised (dots3). Direct reload (#64336) also needs every checkpoint tensor to have a registered place to live.

**Design.** Each checkpoint tensor is a parameter under its checkpoint name and loads on its own. Post-load processing combines the parts in place, so addresses stay stable for CUDA graphs.

1. **GLM5-next FP8 MLA projections.** New `Fp8DequantConfig` / `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` (`layers/quantization/fp8_dequant.py`) for layers that a checkpoint stores as block FP8 but that run in BF16.
   - The weight is the BF16 weight. An FP8 tensor loads through an FP8 view of the same storage (row *i* into the first half of BF16 row *i*'s bytes), so no memory is added. Post-load processing dequantizes those rows in place, in chunks; BF16 rows and dummy weights are left alone.
   - `weight_scale_inv` is a regular block scale, retired after processing but registered for reloads.
   - `fp8_rows` (host bookkeeping on the CPU) marks the rows loaded as FP8, so post-load processing dequantizes only those.
   - The scale starts as `FP8_SCALE_SENTINEL`; at cold start, post-load processing raises if an FP8 row's scale never arrived. On a direct reload, a missing scale is caught by the update-completeness check (#54477 F2) instead.
   - Loaders only adapt single tensors: the Quark `weight_scale` name and NoPE `kv_a` padding. A BF16 tensor needs no scale; `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` marks its `weight_scale_inv` `optional_in_checkpoint`, which the opt-in strict loaded-weights check (`enable_weights_track`, `default_loader.py`) honours, so BF16 checkpoints don't report it as missing (also when the GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM wraps the layer).
2. **Indexer `wk`** (DeepSeek-V2/V3.2, HY-V4, GLM5-next, their MTPs, dots3). `wk_weights_proj` uses `Fp8DequantLinearMethod`. Checkpoints store the `wk` scale as 128×128 blocks, per channel, per tensor or MXFP8 E8M0. The layer is replicated, so its scale is one float32 per row and 32 columns, and each layout is expanded into it as it loads (widths must be multiples of 32, as the indexer's are). The `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` helpers and buffers are removed. The GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM wraps `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` layers, keeping their post-load processing.
3. **MiMo-V2 fused FP8 `qkv_proj`** (model and MTP). The checkpoint is pre-sharded for `num_key_value_heads` ranks.
   - The weight loader writes this rank's rows in the forward's layout; it needs no scale.
   - `weight_scale_inv` holds one checkpoint scale per row; its loader also records whether the rows need requantizing, which depends on the scale tiling.
   - Post-load processing (`_Fp8RowScalesLinearMethod`, adopted from the layer's `Fp8LinearMethod`) turns row scales into block scales in the same storage. Where rows form whole checkpoint blocks it takes each block's scale; otherwise it dequantizes and requantizes as the base did. It raises if the weight was loaded without its scale.
   - Both tensors are written with `default_weight_loader`, as on main; the MTP's BF16 fused branch is unchanged from main.

**Known limitations**
- MiMo `qkv_proj` must be in every update, like any block-FP8 linear layer: its post-processing (DeepGEMM on SM100) rewrites the weight and scales. A direct reload that leaves out its weight, or sends only its scale, post-processes the previous load's bytes without an error here; the update-completeness check (#54477 F2, aoshen02/vllm#176) raises for both before post-load processing runs.
- A bare `model.load_weights` of FP8 tensors without the reload lifecycle leaves FP8 bytes in those rows until post-load processing runs. BF16 tensors load and run as before. This includes the sparse NCCL engine, which runs only `finalize_model_weights` and never the layers' post-load step.
- Layerwise reload is not supported for these layers (it is being removed, #54477). A direct reload that sends FP8 rows without their scale reuses the previous scale; the update-completeness check (#54477 F2) is what rejects that.
- **Sharded RDT is not supported for these models**, on main or with this PR:
  - On main, GLM5-next fails when the engine initializes (`unhashable type: 'list'`), and DeepSeek-V3.2 fails on the second sync (`CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`). FP8 updates into these layers are refused at bake time.
  - This PR leaves the RDT engine unchanged. The fix is the load plan, #64418: its `TraceTensor` replaces the RDT bake and ignores constant writes, and RDT moves onto direct reload.
- **Out of scope: other loaders that pair checkpoint tensors across calls, left as on main because these models are not RL targets:**
  - Molmo / Molmo2 (`molmo.py`, `molmo2.py`): concatenates `wte.embedding` and `wte.new_embedding` in one call. VLM.
  - Flint (`vllm/models/flint/ops/moe.py`, `flint/model.py`): waits for all expert tensors and repacks in the loader; re-reads the GGUF. Niche NVFP4/GGUF.
  - Jina-embeddings-v3 (`bert_with_rope.py`): merges LoRA A/B into the base weight. Embedding model.
  - Reranker conversions: Qwen3-Reranker, mxbai-rerank-v2, bge-reranker-v2-gemma (`adapters.py`). They derive `score.weight` from `lm_head` rows. Pooling models.
  - BERT MLM (`bert.py`): copies the decoder from the embedding when it is absent. Encoder-only.
  - Whisper family: voxtral, ultravox, ming_audio, moss_transcribe_diarize, glmasr (`whisper.py`). They add a zero k_proj bias per call. Audio.
  - Nemotron-3.5 Transcribe (`nemotron3_5_transcribe_audio.py`): checks audio-tower completeness per call. ASR.
  - openPangu (`openpangu.py`): derives the attention sinks per call. Niche.
  - AliceAI (`alice_ai.py`): checks completeness per call. Niche.
  - FoPE / InternS1-Pro (`rotary_embedding/fope.py`): builds its cos/sin cache at the first forward. Niche.
  - ColBERT, ColPali, ColQwen3, ColQwen3.5: their loaders bypass the parameters' weight loaders. Retrieval models.
  - Drafters that are rarely updated: Qwen3 XPress, LiLiCorr, Laguna DFlash, and the Qwen3 DFlash `mask_embedding` (re-read from disk).
  - torchao and humming: direct reload refuses them.

+def _block_fp8(rows: int, cols: int, seed: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)

+"""Block-FP8 checkpoint weights for linear layers that run in BF16.
+
+Some models keep a projection in BF16 although their FP8 checkpoint stores it
+as block-FP8 (``weight`` + ``weight_scale_inv``). The weight and its scale are
+registered under their checkpoint names and loaded independently, in any order
+and in any number of ``load_weights`` calls; post-load processing dequantizes
+them. A BF16 tensor under the weight's name (a BF16 checkpoint, or a trainer
+sending BF16 weights) is loaded as is and needs no scale.
+
+Each FP8 row sits in the first half of the bytes of its BF16 row, so the
+weight's storage is the size of the BF16 weight and every row can be loaded as
+either format, even within one fused weight.
+
+A replicated layer may also accept its scale in any layout a checkpoint uses
+(per-tensor, per-channel, blocks, MXFP8): the scale is then kept as one value
+per row and 32 columns, the finest of these layouts, and a coarser checkpoint
+scale is expanded to it when loaded.
+"""
+

+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import (
+    LinearBase,
+    MergedColumnParallelLinear,
+    ReplicatedLinear,
+    UnquantizedLinearMethod,
+    register_weight_loader_v2_supported_method,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import QuantizationMethods
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.base_config import (
+    QuantizationConfig,
+    QuantizeMethodBase,
+)

+    FP8_SCALE_SENTINEL,
+    create_fp8_scale_parameter,
+    validate_fp8_block_shape,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.parameter import (
+    BlockQuantScaleParameter,

+    is_weights_pre_processed,
+    retire_parameter,
+    set_weight_attrs,
+)
+
+# Rows dequantized at once; bounds the float32 temporaries of a large weight.
+_DEQUANT_ROWS = 1024
+# Scale blocks of a weight that accepts any checkpoint scale layout.
+_ANY_LAYOUT_BLOCK = [1, 32]
+
+
+def _set_data(param: torch.nn.Parameter, tensor: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    # assigning `self.data` inside the subclass trips mypy's [has-type]
+    param.data = tensor
+
+
+class Fp8DequantWeightParameter(ModelWeightParameter):
+    """A ``[rows, cols]`` BF16 weight loadable from block-FP8 or BF16 rows.
+
+    An FP8 tensor loads through `fp8_view`, the same storage in the
+    checkpoint's layout; ``fp8_rows`` (on the host) marks the rows whose bytes
+    are FP8 and still need dequantizing. Rows loaded as BF16, or never loaded
+    (dummy weights), hold runtime bytes."""
+
+    fp8_rows: torch.Tensor
+
+    def fp8_view(self) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """The weight's storage in the checkpoint's FP8 layout: row i in the
+        first half of the bytes of BF16 row i."""
+        data = self.data
+        rows, cols = data.shape
+        view = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device=data.device)
+        offset = data.storage_offset() * data.element_size()
+        return view.set_(data.untyped_storage(), offset, (rows, cols), (2 * cols, 1))
+
+    def _load(self, load, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor, **kwargs):
+        fp8 = loaded_weight.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        if fp8:
+            runtime = self.data
+            _set_data(self, self.fp8_view())
+            try:
+                load(loaded_weight, **kwargs)
+            finally:
+                _set_data(self, runtime)
+        else:
+            load(loaded_weight, **kwargs)
+        rows = slice(None)  # the whole weight, or a merged / qkv shard's rows
+        if "shard_offset" in kwargs:
+            start = kwargs["shard_offset"]
+            rows = slice(start, start + kwargs["shard_size"])
+        # loader state read by post-load processing
+        self.fp8_rows[rows] = fp8
+

+        self._load(super().load_column_parallel_weight, loaded_weight)
+
+    def load_replicated_weight(self, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor):
+        self._load(self._assert_and_load, loaded_weight)

+        self._load(super().load_merged_column_weight, loaded_weight, **kwargs)
+

+        self._load(super().load_qkv_weight, loaded_weight, **kwargs)

+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def dequantize(self, scale_inv: torch.Tensor, block_size: list[int]) -> None:
+        """Dequantize the FP8 rows in place. Every row then holds runtime
+        bytes, so a later reload that leaves this weight out keeps them."""
+        if not self.fp8_rows.any():  # host flags: no device sync
+            return
+        runtime = self.data
+        fp8 = self.fp8_view().view(torch.uint8)
+        block_n, block_k = block_size
+        rows = self.fp8_rows.nonzero().flatten().to(runtime.device)
+        blocks = rows // block_n
+        if (scale_inv[blocks] == FP8_SCALE_SENTINEL).any():
+            raise ValueError(
+                "FP8 weight rows were loaded without their weight_scale_inv"
+            )
+        for index in rows.split(_DEQUANT_ROWS):
+            # gathered before writing: BF16 row i overwrites FP8 row i
+            weight = fp8[index].view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).to(torch.float32)
+            scale = scale_inv[index // block_n].to(torch.float32)
+            scale = scale.repeat_interleave(block_k, dim=1)[:, : weight.shape[1]]
+            runtime[index] = (weight * scale).to(runtime.dtype)
+        self.fp8_rows.zero_()
+

+def _scale_groups(scale: torch.Tensor, rows: int, cols: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The checkpoint scale of a ``[rows, cols]`` FP8 weight, in any layout
+    (per-tensor, per-channel, ``[n, k]`` blocks, MXFP8 E8M0), as one float32
+    scale per row and ``_ANY_LAYOUT_BLOCK[1]`` columns."""
+    group = _ANY_LAYOUT_BLOCK[1]
+    if scale.dtype in (torch.uint8, torch.float8_e8m0fnu):
+        scale = scale.view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu)
+    scale = scale.to(torch.float32)
+    scale = scale.reshape(scale.shape[0] if scale.ndim else 1, -1)
+    block_n, block_k = rows // scale.shape[0], cols // scale.shape[1]
+    if (
+        block_n * scale.shape[0] != rows
+        or block_k * scale.shape[1] != cols
+        or (block_k % group and scale.shape[1] > 1)
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"unsupported scale shape {tuple(scale.shape)} for a "
+            f"[{rows}, {cols}] FP8 weight"
+        )
+    columns = torch.arange(0, cols, group, device=scale.device) // block_k
+    return scale.repeat_interleave(block_n, dim=0)[:, columns]

+    expanded before it is sliced, so it must hold the whole shard's rows."""

+        rows = kwargs["shard_size"]  # weight rows: one scale row per row
+        loaded_weight = _scale_groups(loaded_weight, rows, self.cols)
+        super().load_merged_column_weight(loaded_weight, **kwargs)
